docs.title: Use docs programmatically
docs.heading_path: Use docs programmatically
docs.snippet: We want to make our documentation as accessible as possible. We've included several ways for you to use these docs programmatically through AI assistants, code editors, and direct integrations, such as Model Context Protocol (MCP).

docs.title: Quick access options
docs.heading_path: Use docs programmatically > Quick access options
docs.snippet: On any page in our documentation, you'll find a contextual menu dropdown in the top right corner:

docs.title: Use our MCP servers
docs.heading_path: Use docs programmatically > Use our MCP servers
docs.snippet: Our documentation exposes two complementary **Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers** that let AI applications query LangChain content in real-time. For the best results, we recommend connecting both:

docs.title: Connect with Claude Code
docs.heading_path: Use docs programmatically > Use our MCP servers > Connect with Claude Code
docs.snippet: If you're using Claude Code, run these commands in your terminal to add both servers to your current project:

docs.title: Connect with Claude Desktop
docs.heading_path: Use docs programmatically > Use our MCP servers > Connect with Claude Desktop
docs.snippet: 1. Open Claude Desktop 2. Go to Settings > Connectors 3. Add both MCP server URLs:  * https://docs.langchain.com/mcp  * https://reference.langchain.com/mcp

docs.title: Connect with Codex CLI
docs.heading_path: Use docs programmatically > Use our MCP servers > Connect with Codex CLI
docs.snippet: If you're using OpenAI Codex CLI, run these commands in your terminal to add both servers globally:

docs.title: Connect with Cursor
docs.heading_path: Use docs programmatically > Use our MCP servers > Connect with Cursor
docs.snippet: json theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}} {  "mcpServers": {  "docs-langchain": {  "url": "https://docs.langchain.com/mcp"  },  "reference-langchain": {  "url": "https://reference.langchain.com/mcp"  }  } }

docs.title: Connect with Deep Agents Code
docs.heading_path: Use docs programmatically > Use our MCP servers > Connect with Deep Agents Code
docs.snippet: Add both servers to your user-level ~/.deepagents/.mcp.json file to make them available in every Deep Agents Code project, or add them to a project-level .mcp.json file for only that project:

docs.title: Connect with VS Code
docs.heading_path: Use docs programmatically > Use our MCP servers > Connect with VS Code
docs.snippet: json theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}} {  "servers": {  "docs-langchain": {  "url": "https://docs.langchain.com/mcp"  },  "reference-langchain": {  "url": "https://reference.langchain.com/mcp"  }  } }

docs.title: Connect with Antigravity
docs.heading_path: Use docs programmatically > Use our MCP servers > Connect with Antigravity
docs.snippet: json theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}} {  "mcpServers": {  "docs-langchain": {  "serverUrl": "https://docs.langchain.com/mcp"  },  "reference-langchain": {  "serverUrl": "https://reference.langchain.com/mcp"  }  } }

docs.title: Approval modes
docs.heading_path: Approval modes
docs.snippet: > Choose how Deep Agents Code reviews gated tool calls with Manual, Auto, and YOLO modes

docs.title: Choose a mode
docs.heading_path: Approval modes > Choose a mode
docs.snippet: <Warning>  Auto is an authorization heuristic for a local coding agent. It is **not** sandbox containment, an operating-system boundary, or a guarantee that model-generated actions are safe. </Warning>

docs.title: Enable Auto
docs.heading_path: Approval modes > Enable Auto
docs.snippet: <Steps>  <Step title="Launch with Auto" icon="terminal">  bash theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}}  dcode -y

docs.title: Enable YOLO
docs.heading_path: Approval modes > Enable YOLO
docs.snippet: YOLO runs gated actions without any review. Use it only when you accept that the agent can take any action without asking.

docs.title: How Auto works
docs.heading_path: Approval modes > How Auto works
docs.snippet: Auto keeps the same gated-action rules as Manual but changes how those actions are reviewed. It uses two stages:

docs.title: Select a classifier model
docs.heading_path: Approval modes > How Auto works > Select a classifier model
docs.snippet: By default, the Auto classifier uses the same model as the main agent. You can point it at a different (typically cheaper and faster) model to reduce cost and latency during Auto review.

docs.title: Revalidate before side effects
docs.heading_path: Approval modes > How Auto works > Revalidate before side effects
docs.snippet: The decision plan is bound to the thread, mode, batch, and exact gated calls. Missing or invalid state, a mode race, or a replay falls back to human review. For example, if you switch to Manual while classifier review is in progress, an earlier Auto decision cannot execute…

docs.title: Understand scope and limitations
docs.heading_path: Approval modes > How Auto works > Understand scope and limitations
docs.snippet: * The Manual approval menu can enable Auto for the current thread. Threshold fallback can switch permanently to Manual or perform a one-off review while leaving Auto enabled. * The active model is not an independent security authority. MCP read-only annotations are trusted as a…

docs.title: Where Auto and YOLO are available
docs.heading_path: Approval modes > Where Auto and YOLO are available
docs.snippet: Auto and YOLO are interactive-mode features. Auto is eligible only in an interactive, unsandboxed session; a remote --sandbox forces it to Manual. YOLO is interactive-only as well and requires the risk acknowledgement regardless of sandbox. Headless runs use fail-closed MCP…

docs.title: Remember the last mode across sessions
docs.heading_path: Approval modes > Where Auto and YOLO are available > Remember the last mode across sessions
docs.snippet: When no flag or configured mode applies, Deep Agents Code restores the last selected Manual or Auto mode. YOLO must be explicitly selected. See Startup approval mode.

docs.snippet: Use -n/--non-interactive to run a single task without the interactive UI. Each non-interactive run starts a fresh thread; file-based state (memory, skills, configuration) persists across invocations:

docs.snippet: ~/.deepagents/config.toml lets you customize model providers, set defaults, and pass extra parameters to model constructors. For environment variables and inspection commands, see Configuration. This page covers:

docs.title: Session cost warning
docs.heading_path: Config file > Session cost warning
docs.snippet: Deep Agents Code warns once per thread when its cumulative estimated cost exceeds \$50 and suggests using /offload or /clear. You can configure the threshold in USD, or set it to 0 or a negative value to disable the warning:

docs.title: Cold prompt-cache warning
docs.heading_path: Config file > Cold prompt-cache warning
docs.snippet: Some LLM providers automatically cache the conversation prefix between turns, so a follow-up sent while the cache is warm re-processes only new tokens. That cache expires after a provider-specific idle window. Deep Agents Code currently detects this for Anthropic and OpenAI…

docs.title: Trust a gateway endpoint for cache policies
docs.heading_path: Config file > Cold prompt-cache warning > Trust a gateway endpoint for cache policies
docs.snippet: If requests reach the provider through a gateway or proxy instead of the official API, the cold-cache warning stays silent. Declaring an endpoint trusted asserts that it forwards cache settings untouched and honors the provider's documented retention:

docs.title: Show provider-visible reasoning
docs.heading_path: Config file > Show provider-visible reasoning
docs.snippet: Provider-visible reasoning is hidden by default. To show it in the interactive transcript and non-interactive output, set:

docs.title: Diff line numbers
docs.heading_path: Config file > Diff line numbers
docs.snippet: Deep Agents Code shows file-relative line numbers in transcript and approval diffs by default. To hide them, set:

docs.snippet: <ResponseField name="api_key_env" type="string" post={["optional"]}>  The **name** of the environment variable that holds the API key (e.g., "OPENAI_API_KEY"). Deep Agents Code reads the credential from this env var at startup to verify access before creating the model.

docs.snippet: <ResponseField name="profile" type="object" post={["optional"]}>  (Advanced) Override fields in the model's runtime profile (e.g., max_input_tokens). Flat keys apply to every model from this provider. Model-keyed sub-tables (e.g., [profile."claude-sonnet-4-5"]) override…

docs.heading_path: Config file > Model constructor params
docs.snippet: The params field forwards extra arguments to the model constructor. To give one model different values, add a model-keyed sub-table so you do not have to duplicate the whole provider config:

docs.title: Retries
docs.heading_path: Config file > Retries
docs.snippet: Deep Agents Code retries transient model errors at the model node. The default is five retries after the first request. Set the top-level [retries] value to change the budget, or set it to 0 to disable retries:

docs.title: Startup approval mode
docs.heading_path: Config file > Startup approval mode
docs.snippet: Set the default approval mode for interactive sessions with the top-level [startup].mode key:

docs.title: Auto classifier timeout
docs.heading_path: Config file > Auto classifier timeout
docs.snippet: When Auto mode is active, the classifier has a time budget to review each batch of gated actions. Batches not reviewed within the deadline are denied as classifier_unavailable; repeated misses fall back to the manual approval UI. The default is 20 seconds.

docs.title: Profile overrides (Advanced)
docs.heading_path: Config file > Profile overrides (Advanced)
docs.snippet: Override fields in the model's runtime profile to change how Deep Agents Code interprets model capabilities. See ModelProfile for the full list of overridable fields. The most common use case is lowering max_input_tokens to trigger auto-summarization earlier—useful for testing…

docs.title: Apply to all models from this provider

docs.heading_path: This model gets a higher limit > Adding models to the interactive switcher
docs.snippet: Some providers (e.g. langchain-ollama) do not bundle model profile data (see Provider reference for full listing). When this is the case, the interactive /model switcher will not list models for that provider. You can fill in the gap by defining a models list in your config file…

docs.snippet: Some provider packages accept a base_url to override the default endpoint. For example, langchain-ollama defaults to http://localhost:11434 via the underlying ollama client. To point it elsewhere, set base_url in your configuration:

docs.snippet: Deep Agents Code works with any tool calling LLM available as a LangChain BaseChatModel. The built-in providers work out of the box; a less common or in-house model takes a little more setup. Point class_path at its BaseChatModel subclass and Deep Agents Code imports and…

docs.snippet: With this config, switch to the model with /model xyz:abc-xyz-1 or --model xyz:abc-xyz-1.

docs.snippet: An API key and the endpoint it is sent to have to match: the endpoint has to accept that key, or the request will likely fail. Deep Agents Code resolves the key and endpoint together, so overriding one updates the other to match. For example, if you replace a gateway-provisioned…

docs.snippet: When you store a key with /auth, the endpoint you enter (or the provider's default, if left blank) is applied together with the key. Storing a key with a blank base URL also clears any endpoint already set in your environment (for example, a gateway OPENAI_BASE_URL your shell…

docs.snippet: On a machine provisioned with a model gateway (for example, the LangSmith gateway), the gateway typically exports a gateway key and the matching endpoint variable (OPENAI_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, or GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL) together. Deep Agents Code uses that pair by…

docs.heading_path: This model gets a higher limit > JS interpreter
docs.snippet: The [interpreter] section tunes the built-in JavaScript interpreter (the js_eval tool), which runs agent-written code in a QuickJS sandbox. These keys apply only to config files; see Command line options for the --interpreter and --interpreter-tools flag equivalents.

docs.snippet: The [extensions] section controls Python extension discovery and project trust. The experimental feature gate is required even when extension loading is enabled here.

docs.snippet: The LangGraph graph step budget is the maximum number of node invocations the dcode agent graph may execute in a single turn. Configure this recursion limit with the [runtime] section:

docs.snippet: > Configure Deep Agents Code with config files, administrator settings, environment variables, hooks, and CLI flags

docs.title: How settings resolve
docs.heading_path: Configuration > How settings resolve
docs.snippet: Deep Agents Code uses tiered configuration. The precedence order depends on the setting type.

docs.title: Inspect configuration
docs.heading_path: Configuration > Inspect configuration
docs.snippet: The dcode config commands show the settings Deep Agents Code uses and where each value comes from, without starting a session. Use them to confirm that an administrator setting, environment variable, or config.toml setting is active.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.heading_path: Configuration > Environment variables
docs.snippet: In addition to shell exports, Deep Agents Code reads environment variables from dotenv files, so you can keep API keys out of your shell profile and avoid duplicating .env files across projects.

docs.title: Loading order and precedence
docs.heading_path: Configuration > Environment variables > Loading order and precedence
docs.snippet: At startup, Deep Agents Code reads the nearest project .env, found by searching the directory you launch from and walking up through its parents (the first .env found wins), then ~/.deepagents/.env as a global fallback for all projects. A project .env wins over the global one,…

docs.title: `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_` prefix
docs.heading_path: Configuration > Environment variables > `DEEPAGENTS_CODE_` prefix
docs.snippet: All Deep Agents Code-specific environment variables use a DEEPAGENTS_CODE_ prefix (e.g., DEEPAGENTS_CODE_AUTO_UPDATE, DEEPAGENTS_CODE_DEBUG). See the environment variable reference for the full list.

docs.title: Skill directory allowlist
docs.heading_path: Or set it empty so Deep Agents Code ignores a key exported in your shell > Skill directory allowlist
docs.snippet: By default, when Deep Agents Code loads skills it validates that a resolved skill file path stays inside one of the standard skill directories. This prevents symlinks inside skill directories from reading arbitrary files outside those roots.

docs.title: Profile location (`DEEPAGENTS_HOME`)
docs.heading_path: Or set it empty so Deep Agents Code ignores a key exported in your shell > Profile location (`DEEPAGENTS_HOME`)
docs.snippet: DEEPAGENTS_HOME selects the directory Deep Agents Code uses as its user profile — everything normally stored under ~/.deepagents/ moves under the configured path. This includes config.toml, the global .env, ~/.deepagents/.mcp.json and hooks.json, extensions/, per-agent…

docs.title: Themes
docs.heading_path: Or set it empty so Deep Agents Code ignores a key exported in your shell > Themes
docs.snippet: Use /theme to open an interactive theme selector. Navigate the list to preview themes in real-time, press Enter to persist your choice to config.toml.

docs.snippet: Managed configuration lets administrators control Deep Agents Code settings across a fleet. Deep Agents Code checks the administrator-owned managed_config.toml before user environment variables and config, so users cannot override settings defined there.

docs.title: Precedence rules
docs.heading_path: Show diagnostics in the terminal > Data locations > Precedence rules
docs.snippet: When the same item exists in multiple locations, **higher precedence wins completely** (no merging).

docs.title: Skills
docs.heading_path: Show diagnostics in the terminal > Data locations > Precedence rules > Skills
docs.snippet: 1. ~/.deepagents/{agent}/skills/ — User Deep Agents Code 2. ~/.agents/skills/ — User tool-agnostic 3. .deepagents/skills/ — Project Deep Agents Code 4. .agents/skills/ — Project tool-agnostic *(highest)*

docs.title: Subagents
docs.heading_path: Show diagnostics in the terminal > Data locations > Precedence rules > Subagents
docs.snippet: 1. ~/.deepagents/{agent}/agents/ — User-level 2. .deepagents/agents/ — Project-level *(highest)*

docs.title: Instructions
docs.heading_path: Show diagnostics in the terminal > Data locations > Precedence rules > Instructions
docs.snippet: 1. Package base prompt *(always loaded)* 2. ~/.deepagents/{agent}/AGENTS.md *(appended)* 3. .deepagents/AGENTS.md *(appended)* 4. AGENTS.md at project root *(appended)*

docs.title: `.deepagents` vs `.agents`
docs.heading_path: Show diagnostics in the terminal > Data locations > `.deepagents` vs `.agents`
docs.snippet: <Tip>  Use .agents/skills/ for skills that work with any AI coding assistant.  Use .deepagents/skills/ for skills that rely on Deep Agents-specific tools or conventions. </Tip>

docs.title: Cleaning up
docs.heading_path: Show diagnostics in the terminal > Data locations > Cleaning up
docs.snippet: <Warning>  Deleting ~/.deepagents/.state/sessions.db will remove all conversation history and checkpoints.

docs.title: Python extensions
docs.heading_path: Python extensions
docs.snippet: Python extensions customize the dcode agent server without modifying dcode itself. Use them to register model tools, LangChain middleware, virtual storage routes.

docs.title: Create an extension
docs.heading_path: Python extensions > Create an extension
docs.snippet: An extension entry file must expose an asynchronous extension setup function. dcode passes an ExtensionAPI registrar with read-only session context and methods for adding capabilities.

docs.title: Register capabilities
docs.heading_path: Python extensions > Register capabilities
docs.snippet: * d.cwd: Working directory for the session. * d.mode: interactive or headless. * d.has_ui: Whether the session has an interactive terminal UI. * d.path: Entry file for the extension.

docs.title: Register middleware
docs.heading_path: Python extensions > Register capabilities > Register middleware
docs.snippet: Register LangChain middleware to add model or tool behavior to the agent. dcode loads middleware when it builds the agent graph.

docs.title: Register tools
docs.heading_path: Python extensions > Register capabilities > Register tools
docs.snippet: python theme={"theme":{"light":"catppuccin-latte","dark":"catppuccin-mocha"}} from deepagents_code.extensions import ExtensionAPI

docs.title: Route virtual storage
docs.heading_path: Python extensions > Register capabilities > Route virtual storage
docs.snippet: Backend route prefixes must be lowercase absolute paths with leading and trailing slashes, such as /memories/ or /company/knowledge/. dcode rejects invalid paths and routes that overlap its internal artifact or conversation-history storage.

docs.title: Apply runtime changes
docs.heading_path: Python extensions > Register capabilities > Apply runtime changes
docs.snippet: Tools registered after startup appear on the next model request. Middleware and backend routes change agent graph construction and require /reload. Run /extensions to list registrations, their source paths and scopes, load failures, and whether a restart is required.
